summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package is a shim with no functional code: its main module exports a Proxy that returns a no-op function for every property, so any import of the scoped name succeeds silently. A postinstall script (beacon.cjs) and the main module both POST host-identifying data — package name, os.hostname(), __dirname install path, process.cwd(), and process.version — to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The beacon fires automatically on npm install via the postinstall lifecycle hook and again on require() of the main entry, with no opt-in and no documentation. The destination is not a first-party or vendor-affiliated host, and the scoped name resembles a legitimate component library, consistent with a dependency-confusion / typosquat reconnaissance beacon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
